note: Generated from the libFuzzer logs of the runs below by a throwaway script; not run in CI. Targets live in next/crates/dr-doc/fuzz (see its README).
build: cargo +nightly build --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin with cargo-fuzz's RUSTFLAGS (sancov + AddressSanitizer)

runs.when: after the tree fix, full-length inputs

findings.what: Loro's import_batch decodes blobs without checking their checksum; a corrupted blob made the change-header RLE decoder request a 28.7 GB allocation (libFuzzer out-of-memory), which would abort the app.
findings.where: loro-internal 1.17.1: LoroDoc::import_batch -> decode_import_blob_meta(check_checksum = false) -> block_meta_encode::decode_changes_header -> serde_columnar AnyRleDecoder::take_n_finalize
findings.fix: dr-doc checks every blob with LoroDoc::decode_import_blob_meta(bytes, true) before import_batch (core.rs Core::load, ProseReader::load_at, BookReader::load_at); test corrupted_bytes_are_an_error_not_a_crash. Replaying the crashing input after the fix returns an error.
findings.upstream: not reported (outward-facing; left to the supervising session)

findings.what: An anchor decoded from damaged bytes named a container that does not exist; resolving it called LoroDoc::get_text, which panics for a missing container ('The container does not exist in the document').
findings.fix: Anchor::resolve only accepts cursors into the view's own body text (ContainerTrait::id) and reads the length from that text; anything else resolves to None (unlocated). Test anchors_into_another_container_read_as_unlocated. Replaying the crashing input after the fix exits cleanly.
findings.upstream: not reported (left to the supervising session)
